draft.title: The Gallipoli landing
card: On 25 April 1915, Australian and New Zealand troops landed on the Gallipoli peninsula in Turkey. Turkey was part of the Ottoman Empire, which was fighting against Britain and France.
The Allies wanted to open a sea route through the Dardanelles strait to Russia, their ally. Russia needed supplies, and the Ottoman Empire controlled the strait.
The troops landed at dawn, in the wrong place, below steep cliffs and rough ridges. Ottoman defenders held the high ground and fired down on them.
The Anzacs (Australian and New Zealand Army Corps) could not advance far inland. They were held on a narrow strip of coast, and the plan to move quickly failed.
draft.remember: The landing aimed to open a sea route to Russia, but steep ground and Ottoman defenders held the Anzacs on the coast.

a.q: Why did the Allies send troops to land at Gallipoli in 1915?
opts: To open a sea route to their ally Russia
To capture the German capital of Berlin
To defend the coast of Australia from attack
To cut off the Ottoman Empire from Germany by rail
a.why: The Allies wanted to control the strait so supplies could reach Russia by sea. Berlin and Australia were not the targets, because Gallipoli is in Turkey, part of the Ottoman Empire.
a.clue: Think about which ally needed supplies.

b.q: Why were the Anzacs unable to move far inland after landing on 25 April 1915?
opts: Steep ground and Ottoman defenders on high ground held them
They had run out of food and water on the first day
Their own commanders ordered them to stay on the beach
The Ottoman Empire had already surrendered the peninsula
b.why: The landing was below steep cliffs and ridges, and the Ottoman defenders fired down from the high ground. The troops were not ordered to stay put, and the Ottoman forces had not surrendered.
b.clue: Look at where the troops landed and who held the high ground.

a.best: To open a sea route to their ally Russia

b.best: Steep ground and Ottoman defenders on high ground held them
